summary: Instagram is carrying almost all the audience: Hindi videos get hundreds to over 1,400 views there, while YouTube gives most of them under 25 views. The best performers explain a familiar everyday or robot behaviour (motion sensor, robot avoiding walls, street light) with a curious question title, and people share and save them. Weaker videos are near-duplicates (two smoke detector videos, two IR sensor videos, two tap videos) and one English video that only worked on YouTube. Sample size is small and the channel is new, so treat this as early signals.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first Reels about a sensor people meet daily or a robot/maker idea. Title is a 'Kaise...?' or 'X Nahi Dekhta, Phir Bhi...' curiosity question with a surprising twist ('Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', 'Deewar Se Kaise Bachta Hai'), ending with the 🤔 emoji. The 'Robot Deewar Se Bachta Hai' video got the most shares (10) and PIR got the most views, so a relatable behaviour plus a clear 'how does it know' mystery drives sharing and saves.
doMore: Lead with a surprising claim or 'it can't see you, yet...' hook in the first second
Pick robot or maker-project angles (obstacle avoidance, line following, self-balancing) since they earn shares
Publish one topic per sensor, then move on instead of making near-duplicate versions
Post to Instagram first and treat it as the main platform; reuse on YouTube with a Hindi-searchable title
End each video with a share prompt like 'Apne maker dost ko bhejo' to boost shares and saves
stopDoing: Repeating the same sensor with a slightly different title (smoke detector, IR, tap)
Publishing English videos unless you plan a separate English audience test
Choosing abstract topics with no visible everyday moment (TV remote light, ultrasonic) without a stronger hook
